layers.name: base
layers.about: What knows nothing of the server's subsystems: the config, the instance's name and lock. The other base helpers (the clock, text, private files, processes, outbound requests, the environment, the program's name) are the droppen-base crate, outside this check.

layers.name: platform
layers.about: What the subsystems stand on: where the instance keeps its files, the HTTP kit and the origins it answers, the databases, the instance's identity, the OpenAPI extensions, the Claude roots, the supervisor and self-update.

layers.name: domain
layers.about: The subsystems. They may use one another.

layers.name: entry
layers.about: What assembles and serves the subsystems: the router, the app, the web files, the desktop app's settings, shutdown, the command line, and the binary.

allowed.why: A subsystem's routes are typed on api::ApiRouter and read api::AppState, which holds every subsystem's service (and SendResult / SendMessageResult, api's plain answers, sit next to them). They go once each subsystem's routes take an axum FromRef sub-state of their own.
